event-list-planner-project.label: Build an Event List Planner
event-list-planner-project.summary: Build a complete event-list pipeline cumulatively: records, reusable functions, filtering, mapping, and final iteration.

planner_first_record.title: Step 1: Start the event collection
planner_first_record.prompt: Problem: The event planner cannot process a schedule until each event is represented as one structured record. Task: Create `events` as an array containing one event object with `name`, `category`, and `location`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms one correctly shaped event record; the Console stays unchanged.
planner_first_record.hint: Start with one complete record before growing the collection.

help.concept: store one structured record inside an array
help.hint_1: Use one object inside the array.
help.hint_2: Give it name, category, and location.

planner_complete_data.title: Step 2: Complete the schedule data
planner_complete_data.prompt: Problem: One event is not enough to test a real planner, especially filtering across different categories. Task: Keep the first event and add three more event objects with the same `name`, `category`, and `location` shape. Expected result: Check Answer confirms a four-event collection with consistent records; the Console stays unchanged.
planner_complete_data.hint: Preserve the first object and repeat the same record shape.

help.hint_1: Use the same three property names.
help.hint_2: Include at least two Technology events.

planner_category_predicate.title: Step 3: Identify Technology events
planner_category_predicate.prompt: Problem: The planner will need to select only Technology events, so it first needs one reusable yes-or-no rule for a single event. Task: Keep the complete event array and add only `isTechnology(event)` returning whether the category equals `Technology`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the reusable category predicate; the Console stays unchanged.
planner_category_predicate.hint: This function answers one yes/no question.

planner_event_formatter.title: Step 4: Format one event
planner_event_formatter.prompt: Problem: Event objects are useful for code, but a student reading a schedule needs a short line with the event name and location. Task: Keep the data and predicate and add only `formatEvent(event)` returning `name — location`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms one event can be turned into a readable schedule line; the Console stays unchanged.
planner_event_formatter.hint: Transform one record into one display string.

help.hint_2: Use event.location in the same template literal.

planner_filter_events.title: Step 5: Select Technology events
planner_filter_events.prompt: Problem: The planner still contains every category, but this schedule should include only Technology events. Task: Keep every previous function and add only `selectedEvents = events.filter(isTechnology)`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the collection now has a Technology-only subset; the Console stays unchanged.

planner_format_lines.title: Step 6: Format the selected schedule
planner_format_lines.prompt: Problem: The planner has selected the correct Technology event objects, but raw objects are not readable schedule lines for a student. Task: Keep the selected event array and add only `scheduleLines = selectedEvents.map(formatEvent)`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms each selected record has been transformed into readable schedule text; the Console stays unchanged.

planner_show_schedule.title: Step 7: Show every schedule line
planner_show_schedule.prompt: Problem: The schedule lines are ready in memory, but the planner has not shown them anywhere yet. Task: Keep the complete data pipeline and add only a `for...of` loop that logs every line in `scheduleLines`. Expected result: the Console shows one formatted line for each Technology event.
planner_show_schedule.hint: The lines are already selected and formatted.
